shortDescription: Procter & Gamble NYSE:PG is in the spotlight after the consumer products giant unveiled a renewed cost savings program during its Investor Day event on Thursday. children: is in the spotlight after the consumer products giant unveiled a renewed cost savings program during its Investor Day event on Thursday. Notably, the Cincinnati-based company committed to a total of another $10B in cost savings in four years through FY30, mostly focused on using AI capabilities to accelerate speed of execution to deliver higher consumer usage and solve consumer problems. A 20% to 30% reduction in product supply workforce (including contractors) and increased use of automation will also factor in.
plans to reinvest the extra savings in growth while assuming roughly flat headcount and media spending.

During a Q&A session, CFO Andre Schulten reiterated that the main focus is to reinvest in the business to create the volume and scale that leads to higher margins. "We think this is the right approach given the opportunity to tap in more value-conscious consumers who can then uptrade when disposable income improves," noted JPMorgan analyst Andrea Texeira on the update. "We came away confident that PG can count on its strong moats of digital capabilities, supply chain efficiency, and R&D leadership that should continue to reaccelerate the growth to tackle the remaining 21 out of 50 category/country combinations in which P&G needs to improve share," added Texiera.
JPMorgan kept its Overweight rating on Procter & Gamble
moved 1.3% higher in premarket trading to $169.98. The 52-week high is $173.59.

title: Procter & Gamble plans to use AI and automation to free up cash
